name: Cultist
description: A robed figure in tattered crimson vestments stained with old blood and candle wax, the garment's edges worn to frayed threads from creeping through crypt tunnels and kneeling on cold stone. The cultist's face is gaunt and hollow-eyed, pale from weeks spent in the cathedral's lightless depths, their expression a mask of desperate devotion mixed with the haunted look of one who has seen too much of what should remain buried. Around their neck hangs a crude pendant—a fragment of dark crystal or bone carved with necromantic sigils that pulse faintly with absorbed life force. Their hands are stained with grave-dirt and soot, fingernails cracked and blackened from inscribing blood-ritual circles, and at their belt a curved scimitar gleams with an oily sheen, its edge recently sharpened. Dark devotion burns behind their eyes—the fanatic certainty of one who has committed atrocities in service of what they believe is a greater good, beyond charm, beyond fear, beyond redemption.
